title: Per-vector slot bundling pilot with QSA readiness
creator: Aisha Kline
description:
Summary: Pilot a slot-based per-vector pricing model targeted at mid-market and enterprise reranking customers. The pilot combines fixed-size slot bundles (e.g., 10k, 100k, 1M vectors) with conditional volume holdbacks for burst protection and an enterprise QSA/legal checklist to enable sales/contract conversations. Goal is to validate revenue uplift from bundling, measure churn risk vs per-vector, and surface contract items needed for QSA/QSAs and SOC2 procurement.

Proposal details:
- Offer three slot bundle tiers with stepped effective unit price (slot discounts) and optional monthly carryover up to 20% of unused vectors.
- Implement a holdback window: for first 30 days of a new enterprise bundle, allow a 10% soft holdback to prevent extreme initial usage anomalies; this unlocks after anomalous patterns are reviewed.
- Metering semantics: bill on vectors consumed, but allocate consumption from bundles first. For rerank endpoints, normalize per-query vector cost based on candidate set size to avoid double-counting when downstream deduping occurs.
- Enterprise QSA readiness: prepare a short QSA appendix (answers to SOC2-relevant questions) and an operations playbook for on/offboarding bundles and usage disputes.

Why unique: This design focuses on packaging (slot bundling + carryover) rather than purely lowering per-vector price. It also introduces a pragmatic holdback to reduce risk for capacity-constrained serving and protects customers from accidental spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Define and publish bundle SKUs and pricing matrix to sales and billing teams
Instrument metering for slot allocation and carryover logic in billing pipeline
Run pilot with 3 existing customers (two mid-market, one enterprise) for a 60-day window
QSA appendix drafted and reviewed by Security & Legal
Telemetry dashboards: bundle utilization, effective price per vector, churn signal, and disputed charges
success_metrics: Average effective unit price uplift >= 18% compared to baseline negotiated per-vector discounts
< 2% of billing events marked for dispute during pilot
At least one enterprise converts to 12-month reserved bundle by pilot end
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 0-2): finalize SKU matrix, drafting QSA appendix, and implement meter changes in billing sandbox. Phase 2 (week 3-6): instrument telemetry, set up pilot terms in Stripe/Billing, and onboard pilot customers with dedicated CSM. Phase 3 (week 7-10): monitor pilot, run one mid-pilot health review with engineering & finance, collect qualitative feedback. Phase 4 (week 11-12): decision gate (scale / iterate / cancel).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers perceive bundling as complex -> Mitigation: provide simple calculator and one-pager with example usage patterns
Risk: Metering edge-cases around rerank normalization -> Mitigation: Eng to add unit tests and two production canaries before pilot starts
Risk: Holdback causes customer frustration -> Mitigation: transparent opt-in during pilot and SLA for review turnaround (48 hours)
Risk: QSA questions reveal need for additional controls -> Mitigation: security to triage and provide compensating controls, include contingency in timeline
decisions: Pilot will use bundle sizes 10k/100k/1M vectors with suggested list discounts 8%/18%/32% respectively
Carryover capped at 20% of bundle size and expires after 90 days
Holdback applies only for first 30 days and is reversible by CSM upon manual review
Rerank normalization: cost = base_vector_count * (candidate_set_size / median_candidate_set_size) for reporting; billing uses actual vectors consumed but flagged in invoice line-item
